title: Leave breathing room in your day
description: A day packed edge to edge has no room for the unexpected. Small gaps are not wasted time; they are what make the rest of the day workable.

body.heading: Full is not the same as good
paragraphs: Calendars reward filling. Every empty slot can look like an opportunity, until one late meeting or slow bus knocks the whole tightly stacked day sideways.

Breathing room absorbs the shocks. Ten minutes between commitments is time to finish a thought, get a drink, arrive unruffled, or simply do nothing for a moment, which is also a legitimate use of time.

body.heading: Defend a few small gaps
paragraphs: When you plan, deliberately leave two or three short gaps and treat them as booked. If a day is already crowded, shrink a task rather than deleting the gap; the gap is doing a job.
Notice how the day feels with margins in it. Most people find they end less frazzled and, oddly, get no less done, because a calmer mind makes fewer mistakes to redo.

takeaway: Book a few small gaps on purpose, and let the day breathe.
